# AI Prompt Cook Book — Prompt Recipes for Writers and Viral Marketers

> A free, open-source prompt-engineering cookbook by HoKwang Kim (Dennis Kim, former CEO of Cyworld). 70+ reusable "slash code" prompts (`/hook`, `/tone:empathetic`, `/platform:Instagram`, `/persona:CEO`, etc.), paired ChatGPT/Claude examples, and copy-paste recipes for writers, copywriters, SNS viral marketers, and influencers. Written in Korean. Not investment advice — this is a writing and content-marketing resource that lives inside the vibe-investing repository.

The book's core claim is precise and anti-hype: slash codes are **not built-in model commands** — the model sees `/ELI5` and recalls the idiom "Explain Like I'm 5". Codes are **shared abbreviations between a human and an AI**, and they work best when the definition is stated first. The whole book is organized around a cooking metaphor: context = ingredients, codes = seasoning, recipes = combinations, platform formatting = plating, verification = tasting.

Source: https://github.com/gameworkerkim/vibe-investing/tree/main/02.Investment%20Idea%20Column/AI-Prompt-Cook-Book

Author: Dennis Kim — former CEO of Cyworld Z; 28+ years in game security, social platforms, and blockchain; Microsoft Azure MVP 2015–2023; cyber threat intelligence researcher; runs the open research platform VibeQuant (vibequant.cc).

## Three core principles

1. **Define first.** Give the AI the meaning of a code once; afterward a single slash line suffices (see Appendix A code definition sheet).
2. **Codes are seasoning, context is the ingredient.** Without "who, what, why" (audience, subject, purpose), any code produces generic output.
3. **Always taste the result.** The LLM is Excel, not an oracle — `/statistics`, `/quote`, and `/testimonial` in particular must be fact-checked against real sources.

## How the book is organized

- **PART 1 — Kitchen prep.** Ch 0: how slash codes work (three usage modes, base syntax, combination rules, limits, conflict-resolution table, code-selection flowchart, code relationship map). Ch 1: ChatGPT vs Claude differences (markdown headers vs XML tags, where to place long source text, how to give "why", `<example>`/`<constraint>` usage).
- **PART 2 — The 70+ codes.** Ch 2 explanation codes, Ch 3 tone & style codes, Ch 4 content-structure codes, Ch 5 platform-optimization codes, Ch 6 engagement codes, Ch 7 persona codes, Ch 8 special-purpose codes. Each code has an effect, example, and caution note, plus a ChatGPT/Claude side-by-side comparison.
- **PART 3 — Main recipes.** Ch 9: 10 base combination recipes. Ch 10: SNS viral-marketer recipes. Ch 11: influencer/creator recipes. Ch 12: writer/copywriter recipes.
- **PART 4 — Chef's secrets.** Ch 13: Claude 200% usage, Ch 14: ChatGPT 200% usage, Ch 15: failing prompts and how to fix them, Ch 16: the ethics of going viral.
- **PART 5 — Pro kitchen: quality, performance, safety.** Ch 17: Before/After real outputs, Ch 18: evaluation rubric (with gate items), Ch 19: A/B testing and measurement, Ch 20: advanced prompting intro, Ch 21: safety/security/compliance, Ch 22: case-study notes.
- **Appendices.** A: copy-paste code definition sheet, B: full code overview, C: weekly content calendar template, D: model-update regression guide, E: downloadable template kit.

## The code dictionary (by category)

- **Explanation (Ch 2):** `/ELI5`, `/human`, `/story`, `/expert`, `/TLDR`, `/analogy`, `/stepbystep`, `/visual`, `/timeline`, `/beforeafter`
- **Tone & style (Ch 3):** `/hook`, `/reframe`, `/rewrite:GenZ`, `/tone:funny`, `/tone:empathetic`, `/tone:shocking`, `/tone:motivational`, `/tone:formal`, `/descriptive`, `/quote`, `/monologue`
- **Content structure (Ch 4):** `/framework:AIDA`, `/framework:PAS`, `/problem/solution`, `/listicle`, `/compare`, `/table`, `/FAQ`, `/headline`, `/commentbait`, `/summary`
- **Platform (Ch 5):** `/platform:Instagram`, `:YouTube`, `:Blog`, `:Email`, `:TikTok`, `:Resume`, `:Ad`, `:Slide`, `:Podcast`, `:LinkedIn` (extensible to `:Threads`, `:X`, `:NaverBlog`, `:KakaoChannel`)
- **Engagement (Ch 6):** `/quiz`, `/poll`, `/fillintheblank`, `/engage`, `/curiosity`, `/controversial`, `/boldclaim`, `/objection`, `/dialogue`, `/calltoaction`
- **Persona (Ch 7):** `/persona:coach`, `:developer`, `:marketer`, `:designer`, `:student`, `:teacher`, `:CEO`, `:journalist`, `:therapist`, `:investor` (plus `:customer`, `:hater`, `:editor` for review)
- **Special purpose (Ch 8):** `/promptbuilder`, `/actionplan`, `/statistics`, `/testimonial`, `/meme`, `/tweet`, `/oneliner`, `/command`, `/filltemplate`, `/keywordinject`

## Safety rules baked into the book

- `/statistics`, `/quote`, `/testimonial` may fabricate plausible numbers/quotes/reviews — require source attribution or `[확인 필요]` markers; never invent testimonials (consumer deception).
- `/tone:shocking` and `/controversial` must stay within factual bounds — distortion causes reverse-virality (boycotts/reports); pair with `/objection` and use "steelman" counterarguments.
- `/commentbait` and engagement codes should create a *reason* to respond, not beg for engagement (LinkedIn explicitly demotes engagement bait).
- Advertising/sponsorship content must be labeled; regulatory industries require expert review (see compliance checklist in templates/).
- The evaluation rubric treats **factuality** and **legal/ethical risk** as gate items: unless both score 5, the draft is not published regardless of total score.

## Reading paths

- **Writers/essayists:** Ch 1 → 3 → 12. **Copywriters:** Ch 4 → 12 → 15. **SNS viral marketers:** Ch 5 → 6 → 10. **Performance/brand marketers:** Ch 4 → 7 → 10. **Influencers/creators:** Ch 5 → 11 → 16.
- **Beginner track:** copy-paste codes and recipes (Ch 0, 2–8, 9, Appendix A). **Intermediate:** build a repeatable system with scoring/experiments/calendar (Ch 10–12, 17–19, 21, Appendix C·E). **Advanced:** automation via chaining/RAG/API (Ch 13–14, 20, Appendix D).

## Downloadable templates

Located in `templates/`: `code-definitions.md` (Appendix A, paste into ChatGPT custom instructions / Claude project instructions), `rubric.md` (Ch 18 scoring), `compliance-checklist.md` (Ch 21), `regression-test-kit.md` (Appendix D), `content-calendar.md` (Appendix C), and `ab-test-calculator.xlsx`.
